britannica-1911-girishk:
Girishk is a village and fort of Afghanistan, on the right bank of the Helmand, 78 miles west of Kandahar on the road to Herat. The 1911 Britannica entry fixes it 3,641 feet above the sea. Its fort is garrisoned from Kandahar and houses the governor of the district of Pusht-i-Rud.

The fort itself has little military value, the entry says, but the place commands the fords of the Helmand and the road to Seistan, some 190 miles away. It is also the centre of a rich farming district. During the first Afghan War the British occupied Girishk, and a small garrison of sepoys under a native officer held it through a nine-month siege by a far larger Afghan force. Beyond it stretches the Dasht-i-Bakwa plain, toward Farah.
britannica-1911-kushk:
Kushk is a river of Afghanistan. Its name is also borne by the chief town in the Afghan province of Badghis, and by a military post on the border of Russian Turkestan. For part of its course the river forms the boundary between Afghan and Russian territory, though the town stands some 20 miles from the border. The Russian post, called Kushk or Kushkinski Post, is a fourth-class fortress on a branch railway from Merv. The end of that line lies 12 miles to the south, at Chahil Dukteran.

The terminus stands only 66 miles from Herat. In a war it would serve as a base for a Russian advance. Some confusion has grown up over the name Kushk, which people often apply to the terminus. That spot is neither the Russian post nor the old Afghan town. The name thus covers three distinct places.
podcast-dannyjones-gXmLpLeR0hk:
Filmmaker James Fox returns to Danny Jones with what he calls proof that the military held a live alien in Brazil. The case is the Varginha event, in which locals reported strange beings after a crash. Fox has filmed the witnesses for years.

Fox lays out the reports from Varginha, the hospital staff, and the troops said to have moved a being. He argues the proof now goes past rumor. Jones asks what would at last settle the case. Listeners get the full Brazil file from its best known teller. The library files the talk as an archive record, without a verdict.
podcast-joerogan-pb3lyT4T6Hk:
Screenwriter Joe Eszterhas joins Joe Rogan for episode 2508. Eszterhas wrote Basic Instinct and other huge hits of his era. His scripts made him rich and famous in Hollywood.

He shares tales of stars, studios, and the deals behind the films. Rogan draws out stories of a wilder movie age. Eszterhas also reflects on illness and a changed life. The episode gives film buffs a legend's own account of his peak years. Few writers ever held his power, and he tells it like he knows it. His bluntness matches Rogan's own at every turn.
podcast-tuckercarlson-B7oryXsi8hk:
Writer and filmmaker Mike Cernovich joins Tucker Carlson for a strange, wide talk. The title lists his themes: Donald Trump, demons, and hidden federal agents. Few guests mix faith and politics quite like this.

Cernovich argues that agents hide inside the conservative movement itself. He warns friends to watch who urges them toward rash acts. He also speaks of spiritual evil as a real force in public life. Carlson lets the claims run and tests them. The episode will draw listeners who like their politics mixed with mystery and warning.
podcast-tuckercarlson-s2QS8bUNzHk:
Dave Smith joins Tucker Carlson for a rapid-fire tour of Russia, Israel, Trump and the swamp, Obama, and media attacks on Joe Rogan. Smith, the libertarian comic behind Part of the Problem, treats nothing as sacred. His briefing spares no party and no president.

Smith gives his antiwar case on Russia and Israel in quick, sharp strokes. He revisits Obama's legacy and the press campaigns against Rogan and other independent voices. Carlson laughs along while steering the barrage. Bold and laughing viewers get a dissident comic's full clip, aimed at every seat of power.
